dominican-republic.title: Flag of the Dominican Republic

colors.note: Upper hoist and lower fly quarters; symbolises liberty, the sky, and divine protection.
Upper fly and lower hoist quarters; represents the blood shed by liberators.
The central cross and coat of arms background; symbolises salvation and peace.

desc:
- A blue and red quartered field divided by a large white cross, with the national coat of arms at the centre
- The coat of arms features a Bible open to John 8:32, a cross, four Dominican flags, and the motto Dios, Patria, Libertad
- Adopted on 6 November 1863 during the War of Restoration against Spain, based on Juan Pablo Duarte's 1844 design
trivia:
- The only national flag in the world whose coat of arms includes a Bible, open to the verse Y la verdad os hara libres (And the truth shall make you free)
- The design is derived from the flag of Haiti by adding a central white cross and rearranging the colours, reflecting the country's independence from Haitian rule in 1844
- 27 February, the anniversary of the 1844 declaration, is commemorated as Independence Day; the current flag version dates to 1863
